evidence_summary: Tone Machines dates the Nomad Banshee most likely to 1968 and identifies the Nomad and Applied versions as the same product family, while its later September 2025 research says exact manufacturing dates remain unknown. The archive should therefore retain 1968 as a working estimate, not a verified production date.

The Nomad Banshee is described as made under the Applied brand and as part of the Applied Banshee family. Effects Database independently records the Nomad version as Nomad by Applied, but its terminology alternates between Applied Electronics and Applied Audio, so the company-name form should remain qualified in the ledger.

The Nomad Banshee and Nomad Rogue share the same slanted enclosure family and are both documented as Applied-associated products. Tone Machines describes the Rogue as following the Banshee with an added gain stage, supporting a common Applied product lineage, but this does not by itself establish identical production dates for every specimen.

The early Nomad Super Fuzz is documented as a germanium Fuzzrite-type state with unresolved factory origin, while the later Banshee and Rogue are Applied-associated products. The Nomad name therefore cannot be treated as a single-factory indicator across these models.
